why: No wheel option in the catalogue fixes these. wheels4 at r 4.5 with pushing (f 0.5, mu 0.75) climbs about 0.72r = 3.2 cm, short of 5.6. rocker_bogie6 at r 6 might reach 5.6 but stands about 14 cm tall, which breaks under_sofa (9 cm). Wheels would need about 41 cm2 of contact to stay under 0.9 kPa, and a bigger radius only lengthens the patch slightly. Tracks with a 24 cm contact length bridge 0.45 x 24 = 10.8 cm, more than the 9 cm trench. A front idler at 6.5 cm meets the 5.6 cm porch edge. The track top sits at 8.0 cm and the tub top at 3 + 4 = 7 cm, both under the 9 cm sofa. The contact area of roughly 100-150 cm2 at about 0.6 kg gives under 0.6 kPa, so it sinks about 0.6-0.8 cm against a 3 cm belly. The drive stays at gear 100 with motors on hand: two N20s on a 1.8 cm sprocket give about 13 N, against about 3 N for the gravel ramp. Top speed drops to about 0.56 m/s, so 5000 m of lawn takes about 8900 s of the 14400 s allowed. The pack goes to 14.4 Wh (all 6 cells on hand, 12.2 Wh usable) to cover the track's higher rolling resistance and the slower speed, about 9 Wh. Width 11 leaves room for the tracks' side width at the 28 cm garden gate and possibly the bedroom door. The kit costs $14, takes 4 days and 57 machine minutes.

No bump_switch setting gives it any range, and System 1 already tried 32 times (best score 0.93), so the sensor has to be swapped. The HC-SR04 ranges 2 m in any light. That is about 8 times the 0.24 m body length, which removes both the 0.25 m/s limit and the 40 s of back-offs. With no back-offs, 11 m at most of the 0.57 m/s no-load speed takes about 20-25 s, inside 45 s. The camera would not work: in the dark its LED lights only 0.12 m, which is still under the body length. The lidar is not provided. In iteration 1 this same swap gained hallway and lost nothing on the wheeled body. Sensing is independent of the running gear, so it should carry over to the tracked body.
